header: Meeting: Harbor Tech discovery (Quickstart + Security). Date: 2025-12-11. Start: 16:00 UTC. Duration: 54 minutes. Recording: Zoom cloud. Auto-transcription enabled.
summary: High-level discovery for Harbor Tech evaluating Redwood for LLM features. Main focus: time-to-first-token via self-serve API, mapping security constraints for Private/VPC, and establishing quick POC. Customer is leaning PLG first (hosted) but needs clear path to Dedicated/Private for data residency and compliance. Action items and next steps agreed.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
transcript:
00:00:00 - Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I see Priya and team, really appreciate your time. We'll do a quick 45ish minute discovery, cover quickstart and security, and carve out actions. Luca my SE will jump in on perf and infra.
00:00:14 - Priya (CTO, Harbor Tech): Thanks Sofia. We have about 40 squads but we're starting with a small search/assist feature, want to understand how fast we can get tokens flowing and what the path is if this scales.
00:00:28 - Evan (Platform Eng): Also curious about VPC private options - we handle PII sometimes and our legal requires audit logs and customer-managed keys.
00:00:35 - Luca (Redwood SE): Great, we can go through the self-serve API flow, how long to first token, and then outline Dedicated / Private steps. Quick note, Harbor, the free credits usually cover an initial pilot — we'll include a short token allotment and a quickstart repo.
00:00:50 - Marco (Data Eng): How long is it to first token if we just try the hosted API? Minutes? Hours?
00:00:57 - Sofia: Typically it's minutes — sign up, API key in the console, run the SDK sample. We have a one-command curl and SDK snippets (python/js). For many teams it's under 30 minutes to first meaningful response, assuming you have a sample prompt set.
00:01:12 - Dina (Security): When you say sign up, where does the data go and is any of the request text stored? We have to be careful with customer PII.
00:01:20 - Sofia: Good Q. By default hosted calls are processed in our hosted environment; we have configurable retention policies and you can opt out of retention for certain endpoints. For regulated data we usually recommend Private (VPC) or Dedicated with no retention, plus customer-managed KMS if you need.
00:01:36 - Priya: Is Private fully on-prem or VPC? We have hybrid setups.
00:01:41 - Luca: Redwood Private can be deployed in a VPC with a private control plane or as an on-prem bundle for air-gapped. There's some setup work — network peering, certs, and KMS integrations — but once it's up it's the same API surface. Few customers start hosted then migrate to private when compliance needs kick in.
00:02:00 - Evan: For Dedicated, are we reserving GPU capacity? How predictable is throughput?
00:02:06 - Luca: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools — predictable throughput, autoscaling policies, and SLA-backed latency targets. It costs more than hosted per month but you get predictable tail latency. You can also configure burst capacity.
00:02:21 - Priya: Any gotchas on model variants? Like quantized vs full fp16? We need determinism.
00:02:27 - Luca: We surface model variants and quantization profiles in the catalog; for determinism you can pin model versions in the deployment config. Note small differences can happen across kernels — we document perf and quality tradeoffs.
00:02:40 - Marco: Back to quickstart — do you guys have a sandbox dataset or sample prompts to mimic our workload for token estimates?
00:02:48 - Sofia: Yes, we have a reference prompt set and a short benchmark harness. Luca can run a quick sim with your sample set if you share a small representational subset.
00:03:00 - Dina: SOC2, ISO, and audit logs — where do I find those? Also curious about RBAC and SSO.
00:03:07 - Sofia: We have an enterprise security pack: SOC2 report, ISO certs on request, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC at token/route level, and audit logs in Console. I'll share the security pack link. There are also network diagrams for Private deployments.
00:03:22 - Priya: Good. For legal, what about data residency in EU? We need EU-only hosting.
00:03:28 - Luca: We operate regions in NA and EU. For strict residency we'd recommend Private in your EU tenant or dedicated capacity in EU region; hosted EU also possible but verify retention and cross-region fallbacks.
00:03:41 - Evan: Cost — what's the unit economics? We need an estimate for 10k monthly queries, average 150 tokens per query.
00:03:48 - Luca: We can provide a basic cost model, but it hinges on batching, KV caching, and model choice. Redwood Optimize suggestions can show intel about batching and quantization to reduce per-token cost. I'll produce a 1-page cost matrix.
00:04:02 - Priya: Are there prebuilt SDKs for node/python? We want to integrate into a serverless function.
00:04:07 - Sofia: Yes, official SDKs for Python, Node, and Go. There's also an official docker example for edge cases. The SDK handles streaming, function-calls, and auto-reconnect.
00:04:18 - Marco: We might want to test embeddings too for search. Same API?
00:04:22 - Luca: Same API surface, different endpoints. We can share a notebook showing embeddings flow and approximate costs.
00:04:33 - Priya: Ok let's sketch the timeline — we want a POC in <3 weeks. Can Redwood support that?
00:04:39 - Sofia: Yes — self-serve quickstart + credits for week 1; perf benchmark and cost estimate in week 2; if green we can kickoff Dedicated/Private scoping week 3.
00:04:50 - Dina: For the quickstart credits, do they apply to hosted only? Or can we use them for a dedicated demo?
00:04:56 - Sofia: Typically credits apply to hosted. For Dedicated proofs we often do a separate evaluation with cost offsets or trial instances. We'll detail that in the follow-up.
00:05:05 - Priya: A few blockers: SSO must be SAML with SCIM provisioning; audit log retention 1 year; keys in our KMS. Can you do all this?
00:05:15 - Luca: Yes, SAML + SCIM is supported. For KMS we have integrations with Vault, AWS KMS, and HSM options for Private and Dedicated. Audit retention is configurable in Private; hosted has limits but enterprise add-ons extend that.
00:05:32 - Evan: Does Redwood Console expose per-token cost breakdown in real-time? That's important for us.
00:05:38 - Sofia: Yes, per-route and per-token breakdowns, and you can set alerts. It's in Console under usage and cost.
00:05:46 - Marco: Can you do sample latency numbers? Cold-start vs warm?
00:05:50 - Luca: For hosted small models cold-starts are sub-second for streamable paths; larger models will be a couple hundred ms to low seconds depending on sequence length. Dedicated gives tighter 99th percentile. We'll include example p50/p95 numbers in the matrix.
00:06:05 - Priya: Do you do content filtering or moderation? We need to augment our stack.
00:06:11 - Sofia: We provide optional moderation endpoints and safety tooling. Many customers handle post-filtering in their own layers, but optional endpoints exist.
00:06:20 - (crosstalk)
00:06:24 - Dina: Also want to know what logging we can pull into Splunk.
00:06:27 - Luca: Console supports log exports and webhooks; we can push audit logs to your logging pipeline.
00:06:33 - Sofia: Alright, quick demo of sign-up flow? I can screen-share the Console and show the API key creation.
00:06:39 - Priya: Yes please.
00:06:42 - 00:06:42 - (screen share, short pause)
00:06:45 - Sofia: Ok on the Console homepage you see projects, usage, and quickstart cards. Click Create API key, set route permissions, and you get an ephemeral key. There is a free credits banner that will appear if the account is eligible.
00:07:04 - Marco: If we rotate keys does old data still link?
00:07:07 - Sofia: Audit logs will show which key issued calls; rotation is supported and we log key IDs.
00:07:12 - Evan: For SDK integration, do you support streaming to serverless functions without sticky sessions?
00:07:18 - Luca: Streaming uses chunked responses over HTTP/2 or SSE; you can integrate via short-lived connections and our SDK manages reconnect logic. No sticky sessions required.
00:07:30 - Priya: Can we do a quick risk matrix: hosted pros/cons?
00:07:34 - Sofia: Hosted — fastest to ship, lowest ops, great for PLG trials; cons: retention/trust concerns for PII, potential cross-region fallbacks. Dedicated — middle ground: reserved capacity, more isolation, SLA. Private — maximum control, best for regulatory needs but longer setup.
00:07:54 - Dina: For Private, time to deploy? We need an estimated timeline.
00:07:59 - Luca: For VPC-managed Private typically 4–6 weeks with approvals and network setup; on-prem can be 8–12 weeks. We can compress with pre-allocated engineering help.
00:08:12 - Priya: Ok that's helpful. For the POC I want cost + perf and an acceptance criteria: p50 < 200ms for common prompts and 95th < 500ms. Can Redwood meet that?
00:08:23 - Luca: We'll attempt to meet that on dedicated / optimized models. Hosted might be trickier for p95 depending on concurrency. We'll test with your prompt set and report back.
00:08:36 - Sofia: Next steps recap: I'll send quickstart guide, the credits code, and security pack. Luca will run perf tests with a small dataset you send and assemble cost matrix. Dina to send SSO + KMS specifics. We'll aim to reconvene for POC kickoff next Wednesday.
00:08:52 - Priya: Sounds good. Thanks.
00:08:55 - Sofia: Thanks everyone.
00:09:00 - (meeting continues with Q&A, side topics, and minor interruptions; transcript contains periodic timestamps but not full minute-by-minute verbatim due to auto-transcription sampling).
00:45:00 - Sofia: wrapping up — I'll follow up with links and a calendar invite for the POC kickoff.
00:45:10 - Priya: Great.
00:54:00 - (meeting ended)
notes: Customer interested in PLG self-serve first, moving to Dedicated/Private if PII and residency concerns arise. Security-heavy procurement path expected; involve Solutions Engineering and Security early. Preference for short POC with explicit perf SLOs.
